hints: Look at the words 'daylight as a light source'. This tells you the type of microscope, so ask yourself what limits how close two points can be and still be seen separately.
Remember that total magnification (x10 times x40 = x400) makes the image bigger, but it does not change resolution. Resolution for visible light is about half the wavelength of light.
walkthrough:
**Separate magnification from resolution**

Great first check. Total magnification here is $10 \times 40 = 400\times$.

But magnification only enlarges the image. Resolution is the smallest distance between two points that can still be seen as separate.

**Use the wavelength rule for light**

Resolution is limited by the wavelength of the illuminating radiation.

Daylight means visible light, with wavelength about $400-700 \text{ nm}$. The best resolution is about half that wavelength:
$$\text{resolution} \approx 200 \text{ nm}$$

**Choose the matching value and check units**

$200 \text{ nm}$ is the classic textbook value for a high-power light microscope.

$0.20 \text{ nm}$ is $1000\times$ smaller and belongs to electron microscopes. Values in $\mu\text{m}$ are far too large for a resolution limit.

options.A: Too small by 1000 times. About 0.2 nm is the resolution of an electron microscope, not a light microscope using daylight.
options.B: Correct. A light microscope using visible light has a maximum resolution of about 200 nm, set by the wavelength of light.
options.C: Too large. 100 um is about the size of a plant cell, not a resolution limit. Many organelles smaller than this are clearly resolved by light microscopy.
options.D: Too large. 400 um is visible almost with the naked eye, so this cannot be the limit of a x400 microscope.
